confirmed.title: Form inbox / workbook import de-duplication matches DIFFERENT responses submitted a whole number of quarter-hours apart: the second one is silently dropped
confirmed.scenario:
1) A resident has an 'import' case for date D, either from the Admin workbook import or from a drift-repair re-import (like the 72 rows on 14 Oct). Its createdAt is the sheet Timestamp read as UTC, so the real time plus 8 h. Say it was submitted at 09:00:00 SGT.
2) She submits a different Form response for the same date D at 09:45:00 SGT. Any whole number of quarter-hours (±1 s) later works, up to about 22 h.
3) On the next pick-up, mergeFormEntries runs isImportOf against every same-date 'import' case. sameResponse(09:00+8h, 09:45) gives d = 7h15m, a whole quarter-hour, so it returns true.
4) The entry is put in `dupes` and `done`. commitFormPickup deletes formInbox/<id> and writes no case. pickupMessage returns '' for dupes, so no toast is shown.
The reverse case: an Admin workbook re-import (drift repair) of a sheet row the app is missing is dropped by withoutFormCases when any same-date Form case was submitted k×15 min ±1 s apart. The admin log counts it as 'already there'.
confirmed.consequence: A real Form response never reaches the logbook and its inbox entry is deleted, so the pick-up never retries it. The sheet still has the row, so the app's counts are lower than the response sheet's. The drift-repair re-import fails silently for the same reason. The measured false-match rate is 1 in about 300 for each pair of same-date responses within the window. A resident logging several cases for one day gives several such pairs.
confirmed.fix: Accept only the sheet's real offset instead of any quarter-hour: `return [0, 8 * 3600].some(o => Math.abs(d - o) <= 1);`. Make it a constant, or derive it from the import. Optionally also require the same tags or text in isImportOf and withoutFormCases. Add a test with two same-date responses 15 min, 45 min and 2 h apart.
verifier_fix:
In `sameResponse`, accept only the sheet's real offset (Asia/Singapore, +8 h, no DST). Make it a named constant and drop the general quarter-hour tolerance:

`const SHEET_OFFSET_S = 8 * 3600;`
`return isFinite(d) && Math.abs(d - SHEET_OFFSET_S) <= 1;`

Keep offset 0 only if a UTC sheet is a real case. Update the tests:
- remove the "any quarter-hour zone" and "a UTC sheet" assertions;
- add same-date pairs 15 min, 45 min, 2 h and 8 h apart that must not match, in both `mergeFormEntries` and `withoutFormCases`.

Optionally, also require the same category set (cats) in `isImportOf` and `withoutFormCases`. Don't compare details: Form details are ID-masked and an edited response changes them.

confirmed.title: Editing an older Form response creates a second case: the time-based match cannot see edits
confirmed.scenario:
(a) Response R was submitted on 10 Oct, before the inbox went live. It is in the app as an 'import' case whose createdAt is the 10 Oct sheet timestamp + 8 h. On 16 Oct the resident uses her edit link to add a forgotten tag ("Allow response editing" stays ON, owner, 14 Oct). Code.gs fires on the edit and sends formInbox/R. Its submittedAt is the edit time, because getTimestamp moves on edit (the form-inbox.js header comment says so). At pick-up no case with formCaseId(R) exists, and isImportOf compares the 10 Oct stamp with 16 Oct, so there is no match. A new 'form' case is saved next to the import copy.
(b) Response S came in through the inbox. When it is edited, mergeFormEntries keeps the form case's createdAt at the FIRST submission (line 94), but the sheet row's Timestamp moves to the edit time. The next Admin workbook re-import gives the row a new importKey (its timestamp and content changed). withoutFormCases compares the edited timestamp with the form case's first-submission createdAt, finds no match, and writes the row as a second case.
confirmed.consequence: The same Form response is counted twice in the app (summary and Totals): every tag gets +1, while the sheet has one row. All ~16,000 cases from before 14 Oct are 'import' cases, so each edit of an older response adds a duplicate. The duplicates finder does not flag it because the edited copy's text or tags differ from the original. Only the weekly drift check shows it, as app > sheet.
confirmed.fix:
(b) Record the latest submittedAt on the form case, for example importKey `form:<id>@<written>~<submittedAt>` (importKey is a free string ≤200 in the rules), and have withoutFormCases match against it as well as createdAt.
(a) When an entry has no form case and no time match, look for a same-date 'import' case with the same text or the same tags (an edit usually changes only one of them) and replace that case instead of adding one. Failing that, list it in the pick-up toast as 'possibly an edit of an older response' rather than adding it silently. Add both cases to form-inbox.test.mjs.
verifier_fix:
(b) Put the latest submission time before the '@' so `syncedAt` still parses: importKey `form:<id>~<submittedAt>@<written>`. Response ids are [A-Za-z0-9_-], so '~' is unambiguous, and the key stays within the rules' 200-character limit. Alternatively, change syncedAt's regex in the same PR. In withoutFormCases, match a row when it has the same day as a form case and either `sameResponse(row.createdAt, c.createdAt)` or `sameResponse(row.createdAt, latestSubmittedAt(c))`. It would also help to treat the same day, the same normalised caseText and the same cats as a match, because the form case carries the edited content. Note the remaining race: a re-import that runs before the resident's next pick-up still sees only the old content and time.

(a) When an entry has no form case and no time match, look for 'import' cases on the same date (or with the same dateText) whose normalised text equals the entry's text, and act only if exactly one such case exists and it has not been edited in the app. In that case, write the Form's version onto that case's own id: keep its createdAt and the app-only fields (reflectionId, reflectTag, tags), and keep or merge the import key so a later re-import still recognises it. Never match on tags alone. Otherwise, add the entry but list it in the pick-up toast and the logbook flags as "possibly an edit of an older Form response" so the resident can delete one copy. Add tests to form-inbox.test.mjs for an edit of an imported response, an unchanged resubmit, and a re-import after an edit of an inbox-made case. Also add a syncedAt test for the new key format.

confirmed.title: Uploading an Excel file back deletes cases and reverts edits made on other devices when the file came from a stale local copy (exportedAt is the wall clock, not the copy's sync time)
confirmed.scenario:
1) The resident's laptop last synced on Monday. From Tuesday to Thursday she logs cases on her phone and adds a spinal tag to Monday's case b.
2) On Friday she opens the logbook on the laptop without signal (or before the first server snapshot arrives). The sync engine shows the stored Monday copy at once. She taps Download Excel. downloadExcel does not wait for S.casesSynced, unlike the Drive/Dropbox backup (cloud-save.js:72, 'the backup must hold everything') and Markdown sync (ui-sync.js:119). The file gets exportedAt = Friday's Date.now() (xlsxio.js:135).
3) Later, online, she fixes a typo in one row and uploads the file. diffRows lists every case logged Tuesday to Thursday as deleted, and case b as changed back to Monday's tags.
4) The guard keeps only cases with max(updatedAt, createdAt) > exportedAt (Friday), so it keeps none of them. She taps Apply.
confirmed.consequence: Cases logged on other devices go to the recycle bin. Edits made elsewhere are overwritten with the stale version and are not in the bin; in the example a tag is removed, so counts drop. The same zero tolerance also bites when the copy is fresh: a case logged on a phone whose clock runs a few minutes slow, just after the export, is stamped before exportedAt and deleted, although the sync engine allows 10 minutes of skew (SKEW).
confirmed.fix: Stamp the file with the time its cases were last confirmed by the server (the cases engine's meta.syncAt), not Date.now(). Alternatively, make Download Excel wait for S.casesSynced as cloud-save does, and refuse or warn when offline. On upload, compare against exportedAt - SKEW so the skew the sync engine tolerates is tolerated here too.
verifier_fix:
Make the round trip clock-free instead of comparing against a timestamp:
1. **Record the version per row.** On export, write each case's version (updatedAt) next to its id in the hidden id column, or in a second hidden column.
2. **Record which cases the file holds.** List the exported ids in the veryHidden "Export info" sheet, one per row.
3. **On upload, use those records:**
   - Delete a case only if its id was exported and its current updatedAt still equals the exported version.
   - Apply a changed row only if the case's current updatedAt equals the row's exported version.
   - Anything else goes under "Kept (changed elsewhere since this file was made)".
   - Cases absent from the export list are never deleted.
   This covers stale copies, clock skew and writes still in flight.
4. **Older files without this info:** fall back to `min(exportedAt, syncAt) - SKEW` as the cutoff.
5. **Defence in depth:** in the Excel dialog, show a warning when `!S.casesSynced || !navigator.onLine` ("This is the copy last synced on <date>; uploading it back later will keep anything newer"). Don't rely on S.casesSynced alone: it stays true after the connection drops.
6. **Tests:** add a unit test for the stale-copy and skew cases, next to export-opts.test.mjs.

confirmed.title: Later entries of a big Form pick-up are stamped more than 10 s after their importKey, so later edits of those responses are ignored as 'changed in the app'
confirmed.scenario:
1) A pick-up handles many entries, for example after logbookInboxBackfill or after a busy day on the Form. mergeFormEntries(entries, …, now) stamps every case's importKey `form:<id>@now` and updatedAt with one `now`.
2) commitFormPickup commits one batch per entry, one after another, waiting for each server acknowledgement. Already-imported dupes cost a round trip too. For each entry, cleanCase(it.case) stamps updatedAt = Date.now() at that entry's turn.
3) Once the round trips before it add up to more than 10 s (about 40 entries at 300 ms, or one slow or retried commit on hospital wifi), an entry's stored updatedAt > at + SAVE_SLACK.
4) Later the resident edits that response on the Form. The pick-up sees `had.updatedAt > at + SAVE_SLACK`, puts it in `kept`, deletes the inbox entry, and toasts '1 edited Form response left as you changed it here', although she never touched it in the app.
confirmed.consequence: The Form edit never reaches the app, and the inbox entry is gone, so it is not retried. If the edit changed tags, the app's counts differ from the sheet. The toast tells the resident she changed the case herself, which is false.
confirmed.fix: In commitFormPickup, keep the stamp mergeFormEntries chose: `const d = cleanCase(it.case, it.case.updatedAt)`. For an update it is already later than had.updatedAt. Alternatively, rewrite the importKey suffix to `@${d.updatedAt}` after cleaning. Add a test that commits entries with time passing between them.
